commons.title: 'Indian Infantry Company,' Column of Soldiers in Winter Uniforms (fd1093634c724b46ba6b104e514274d8).tif
commons.credit: Unknown Photographer (Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument)
commons.description: LIBI_00312_10951; Albumen photograph, landscape view. This image depicts a company of Native American Infantry formed into a column. The soldiers are wearing the winter uniforms. Tipis are visible in the background. The group may have been acting as a police force. The photo was taken at the Pine Ridge Agency, South Dakota. A white number, “1060” is written on the tree trunk in the image. The photographer may have been George E. Trager or Clarence G. Moorledge. Image was created circa 1890. It may be the original image. There are two holes punched into the right side of the image. ; photograph ;Courtesy of the National Park Service, Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument, LIBI_00312_10951, Unknown Photographer, "'Indian Infantry Company,' Column of Soldiers in Winter Uniforms," circa 1890
commons.editorial_reason: Source category identifies Oglala Lakota; the image shows Native soldiers, winter uniforms, and tipis at Pine Ridge.

commons.title: American photographer Carol M. Highsmith photographs George Free Spirit Medina, a member of the Oglala Sioux tribe, in Pueblo, Colorado, at a gathering of North American Native People LCCN2015633828.tif
commons.description:
Title: American photographer Carol M. Highsmith photographs George Free Spirit Medina, a member of the Oglala Sioux tribe, in Pueblo, Colorado, at a gathering of North American Native People
Physical description: 1 photograph : digital, tiff file, color.

Notes: Mr. Medina is a great-great-great grandson of Chief Crazy Horse, the Oglala Lakota warrior who took up arms against the U.S. federal government to fight against encrochments on the territory and way of life of the Lakota people. Mr. Medina is also of Apache and Mexican heritage.; Forms part of: Gates Frontiers Fund Colorado Collection within the Carol M. Highsmith Archive.; Credit line: Gates Frontiers Fund Colorado Collection within the Carol M. Highsmith Archive, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.; Title, date and keywords based on information provided by the photographer.; Purchase; Carol M. Highsmith Photography, Inc.; 2015; (DLC/PP-2015:068).
commons.editorial_reason: The caption identifies an Oglala Sioux participant, and he is visibly wearing traditional regalia at a Native gathering.
